questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) $1101011_2 + 10111_2$ (2 marks).** Add column by column from the right (the carries are written above the next column; $1+1 = 10_2$ means write 0 and carry 1):

```text
         1111111   (carries)
          1101011
        + 0010111
        ---------
         10000010
```

Right to left: $1+1 = 0$ carry 1; $1+1+1 = 1$ carry 1; $0+1+1 = 0$ carry 1; $1+0+1 = 0$ carry 1; $0+1+1 = 0$ carry 1; $1+0+1 = 0$ carry 1; $1+0+1 = 0$ carry 1; the last carry gives the leading 1.

$$1101011_2 + 10111_2 = 10000010_2$$

*Check:* $107 + 23 = 130 = 10000010_2$.

**(ii) $101100_2 - 111_2$ (3 marks).** Method of two's complement on 6 bits: subtracting $111_2$ is adding its two's complement.

- Write $111_2$ on 6 bits: $000111$.
- Invert every bit: $111000$. Add 1: $111001$. So $-7 = 111001$.
- Add: $101100 + 111001 = 1\,100101$.
- Discard the carry out of the sixth bit: $100101$.

$$101100_2 - 111_2 = 100101_2$$

*Check by borrowing:* column by column from the right, $0-1$ borrows ($10-1 = 1$); $0-1-1$ borrows again ($10-10 = 0$); $1-1-1$ borrows again ($11-10 = 1$); then $1-0-1 = 0$, $0$, $1$, which gives $100101$. In denary $44 - 7 = 37 = 100101_2$. (Checked by a script.)
